title: SIMD-accelerated GF(2^m) dot product using CLMUL batch kernel
description:
Add a SIMD fast path to `FieldVec::dot_product` for `Gf2mElement` that uses the `clmul_batch` kernel from 055bda14.

## Approach

For GF(2^m), the dot product is: multiply each pair (carry-less), XOR-accumulate all products, then Barrett-reduce the final sum once. Since XOR never overflows (`Wide = Self`, `kmax = usize::MAX`), the entire accumulation can be done without intermediate reductions.

The SIMD path:
1. Extract raw `u64` values from both FieldVec slices
2. Call `clmul_batch` to get all 128-bit products in one pass (uses VPCLMULQDQ when available)
3. XOR all products together
4. Barrett-reduce the final XOR sum

This avoids per-element Barrett reduction (saving 2 PCLMULQDQ per element) but pays data marshaling overhead.

## Integration

`simd_dot_product` is implemented as a method on `impl FieldVec<Gf2mElement>` that uses the batch CLMUL path when PCLMULQDQ is available, falling back to the generic `dot_product` otherwise.

## Success criteria

- SIMD dot product produces identical results to scalar path for all m=2..16
- Graceful fallback to scalar when PCLMULQDQ unavailable
- Benchmarks added comparing SIMD batch vs scalar dot product across field sizes

## Code review note: performance comparison

The ≥2× speedup target assumed comparison against a truly scalar (no-SIMD) baseline. However, the generic `dot_product` already uses per-element SIMD via `clmul_barrett_fn` (3 PCLMULQDQ instructions per element in a single target_feature scope, from 055bda14). The batch approach eliminates per-element Barrett reduction (saving 2 PCLMULQDQ per element) but pays data marshaling overhead (extracting u64 values from Arc-wrapped Gf2mElement structs).

Measured results (GF(2^8), n=1000): scalar 10.4 µs, SIMD batch 10.1 µs (~3% faster). The incremental gain from batching over an already-SIMD per-element path is modest. The batch path will show larger gains when:
- Data is already in contiguous u64 layout (SoA representation, tracked in 5fad4d0f)
- AVX-512 provides 4× batch throughput (tracked in c7c0e991)
